at: (English version) to the Commission Cindy Franssen (PPE) (26 March 2024) Subject: Objective of increasing the employment rate by 2030 As part of the March 2021 European Pillar of Social Rights Action Plan, the EU set a target of raising the employment rate to 78% by 2030. 1.
Does the Commission have a clear vision of how it aims to meet that target?

2. What measures have already been taken that are having a significant positive impact on increasing the employment rate in the EU? (6 June 2024) The target that at least 78% of all adults should be in employment by 2030 is one of the three targets proposed by the Commission in the European Pillar of Social Rights Action Plan and welcomed by the EU leaders at the Porto summit and the European Council (1). Member States have defined their 2030 national targets in accordance (2). In 2023, the EU employment rate increased to 75.4%, suggesting that the EU is well on track towards its 2030 target. All Member States made progress towards their national targets compared to 2019, and in several Member States, the employment rates reached levels already higher than the respective targets (3). The Commission supports Member States to achieve the target through the European Semester and policy initiatives, such as the actions proposed in the action plan on Labour and Skills Shortages (4) adopted in March 2024. To make sure that all groups benefit from adequate employment support and participate in reaching the EU target, the Commission will also continue the implementation of the many already adopted EU initiatives, such as the Gender Equality Strategy (5), the reinforced Youth Guarantee (6), the strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities (7) and the action plan on Integration and Inclusion (8). The Commission also supports Member States to achieve the target through financial support, in particular the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) (9) and the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) (10), as well as other funds and programmes such as the Just Transition Fund (11).
